title.en: Similar triangles and Thales (Basic Proportionality) theorem

text.en: At noon a 2 m stick casts a 1 m shadow while a tree casts a 6 m shadow. Because the sun's rays make the same angle, the two triangles have the same shape. How tall is the tree?

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
Thales (Basic Proportionality) theorem: a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
In triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC, AD/DB = AE/EC.
The converse is also true: if a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
The angle bisector of a triangle divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides.
Similarity tests: AA (two equal angles), SSS (three proportional sides) and SAS (one equal angle and the including sides proportional).
For similar triangles, the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides.

problem.en: In triangle ABC, DE is parallel to BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 3, DB = 6 and AE = 2, find EC.

why.en: The parallel line divides the sides proportionally.

prompt.en: State Thales theorem and one test for similar triangles.

requiredIdeas.en: Parallel line divides sides in the same ratio
Areas are in ratio of squares of sides

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the ratio of areas as the ratio of sides

points.en: DE parallel to BC gives AD/DB = AE/EC.
AA, SSS and SAS prove similarity.
Angle bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides.
